title: What is scrap? Start with what you already have.
excerpt: Newspapers, cartons, metal offcuts and old equipment: understand what belongs in a scrap enquiry.
body:
The newspaper stack beside your cupboard. The cartons left after a delivery. The metal pieces from a workshop. Scrap is a useful everyday name for materials or items you no longer need that may have value for reuse or material recovery.

## Look at the material first

Start by identifying what you have: paper, cardboard, a particular metal, plastic, glass, clothing or equipment. Keep different materials separate so the grade and quantity can be assessed clearly.

## An old item may still have a useful life

Consider repair, reuse or donation for something that still works. Recycling is a later step when an item or material can no longer be used in its current form.

## Make the next conversation easier

For an APNA KABADI enquiry, note the material, approximate quantity, condition and pickup access. The guide shows what to prepare, and the rate card identifies whether a price is per kilogram or per piece. Final acceptance and the offer are confirmed before collection.

title: A little sorting. A clearer scrap pickup.
excerpt: Simple preparation can make a household or workplace collection easier to assess and plan.
body:
A scrap pickup begins before the collection vehicle arrives. A few minutes spent separating your items can make it easier to describe the lot and understand the material-wise calculation.

## Keep the categories clear

Set aside newspapers, books and cardboard separately. Keep metals apart where practical. Follow the material guide for the particular item rather than putting everything into one mixed bag.

## Make room without creating confusion

Flatten suitable cardboard boxes and keep paper dry. Keep glass safely packed. Tell us about stairs, large items or restricted vehicle access when you prepare the request.

## Understand the value of your lot

A selling price depends on the actual material, grade and quantity. Check the listed unit, then review the measured quantity and final offer before collection. Larger lots and specific grades can be submitted for a tailored bulk quote. Preparing a request is the start of that conversation; the pickup window still needs confirmation.

title: Why recycling matters after the pickup.
excerpt: Collection is the first step in giving suitable materials another use. Here is the bigger picture.
body:
Recycling involves collecting and processing suitable discarded materials so they can become inputs for new products. A pickup is one step in that wider process, rather than the final outcome.

## Keep useful material in circulation

Recovering suitable paper, metal, glass and plastic can reduce demand for new raw materials and divert material from disposal. The actual outcome depends on sorting, contamination, processing and an available recovery route.

## Reduce and reuse come first

Avoid unnecessary purchases and packaging where you can. Repair or reuse a suitable item before considering recycling. Keeping a useful object in service and recovering its material later are different ways to reduce waste.

## Start with a practical local habit

Keep your scrap categories clear and ask how the particular material will be handled. Electronics and batteries need a separate discussion; they should not be treated like an ordinary paper or cardboard lot. APNA KABADI starts with a Baripada enquiry, a clear material description and an agreed collection plan.
